panel.summary: Undo floor is capture-at-construction only; unlike Slides/Docs there is no `markUndoBaseline()` re-base hook, so a store rebuilt over an already-edited doc silently discards the user's undo history
panel.evidence: `this.undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length` in the constructor is the only capture. YorkieSlidesStore exposes `markUndoBaseline()` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:669) called from slides-view.tsx:648 after a post-construction seed, and YorkieDocStore re-bases in `setDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:732). notes-view.tsx:93 constructs the store in an effect keyed on `[didMount, doc]`; if that effect ever re-runs against the same live doc after local edits, the new floor sits above the user's own units and `canUndo()` returns false for work they can still see. Whether that re-mount can happen today is unclear, hence low confidence — but the missing re-base hook is the divergence from the pattern the issue said to reuse.
panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts::undo floor is capture-at-construction only; unlike slides/docs there is no `markundobaseline()` re-base hook, so a store rebuilt over an already-edited doc silently discards the user's undo history

coderabbit.detail: **Avoid depending on `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` outside tests.** `Document.getUndoStackForTest()` is exposed in `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13, but its `ForTest` suffix indicates it is a test helper, not the stable public history API. Keeping the store’s `undoFloor` calculation tied to this helper makes application code brittle to future SDK changes.
